sections.h2: What do official numbers say about the Texas housing market?
sections.html:
Two federal sources give a clear statewide picture: the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) house price index and Census Bureau QuickFacts. Neither predicts prices, and neither describes one street, so treat them as context for a sale and not as a valuation.

The Census Bureau estimates Texas had 31,709,821 residents on July 1, 2025, up 8.8% from the April 2020 estimates base. It counts 12,848,245 housing units for the same date.

sections.h2: What does the FHFA price index show for Texas?
sections.html:
The FHFA index for Texas stood at 450.76 not seasonally adjusted and 444.25 seasonally adjusted in the second quarter of 2026, with the first quarter of 1991 set to 100. In plain terms, the index says repeat-sale prices in Texas are a little over four and a half times the 1991 starting level.

The index follows price changes in repeated transactions on mortgages that Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac bought or guaranteed. It does not report the price of any one house, so it can differ from what a particular neighborhood experienced, and it tracks repeat sales of the same properties over time. The recent quarters are below.

The seasonally adjusted column moves in a narrow band across these six quarters, between 441.17 and 446.73. Read the pattern as a plateau in the series, and ask a local agent or appraiser what your own area did.

sections.h2: What does Census QuickFacts say about Texas homes and owners?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists the owner-occupied housing unit rate at 62.6% for 2020 to 2024, and the median value of owner-occupied units at $283,800 for the same period. These are survey-based figures for the whole state.

  • Median selected monthly owner costs, 2020 to 2024: $2,106 with a mortgage and $678 without one.
  • Median gross rent, 2020 to 2024: $1,403.
  • Households, 2020 to 2024: 10,992,816, at 2.69 persons per household.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 210,217.
  • Median household income, 2020 to 2024 in 2024 dollars: $78,476.

The gap between the $2,106 and $678 owner-cost medians shows how much of ownership cost is the mortgage. Property tax is part of owner costs on both lines, which is why the tax calendar matters to a seller.

sections.h2: Why are there two columns in the index table?
sections.html:
The not seasonally adjusted column reports raw quarterly values, so it swings with the buying season. The seasonally adjusted column smooths out that pattern, which makes quarter to quarter comparison fairer.

Across the six quarters above, the raw column ran from a low of 439.98 in the fourth quarter of 2025 to a high of 450.76 in the second quarter of 2026. Sellers comparing a spring reading with a winter one should use the adjusted column, and anyone quoting the series should name which column they mean.

sections.h2: How fast is Texas growing, and what does that mean for housing?
sections.html:
Texas added about 2.56 million residents between the April 2020 estimates base of 29,149,498 and the July 2025 estimate of 31,709,821. The 2020 census count was 29,145,505, and the 2010 count was 25,145,561.

Housing supply follows people. Builders took out 210,217 building permits in 2025 according to QuickFacts, and the state counts 111.6 people per square mile as of 2020, against 96.3 in 2010. Over 261,000 square miles of land means growth is uneven: a metro suburb and a rural county can sit at opposite ends of the same statewide average.

QuickFacts gives a few details that shape demand for houses.

  • Persons under 18: 24.0% of the population; persons 65 and over: 14.9%.
  • Veterans, 2020 to 2024: 1,402,357.
  • Living in the same house one year earlier: 86.0% of residents aged one and older.
  • In the civilian labor force: 64.7% of residents aged 16 and over, with a mean commute of 26.7 minutes.
  • Persons in poverty: 13.4%.

The 65-and-older share and the veteran count matter for sellers because both groups can qualify for homestead tax relief, which changes what a buyer inherits in carrying cost. Ask the appraisal district what exemptions are attached to a property before you quote its taxes to a buyer.

sections.h2: Why do median values differ from what homes sell for?
sections.html:
The QuickFacts median is the owners' own estimate of value in a multi-year survey. It lags the market and covers every kind of owner-occupied home, from rural ranch houses to suburban new builds.

The FHFA series is built from transactions, but it is a relative index. It tells you how prices moved against 1991, not what a three-bedroom house is worth today. For a number you can negotiate with, a local comparable sales review or an appraisal does the work that statewide data cannot.

sections.h2: How do property taxes fit into Texas home values?
sections.html:
Property tax is local in Texas, and January 1 is the valuation date. Your bill depends on the value and owner of record that day.

  • Homestead notices of value arrive in spring, so an index reading in the news can be compared with your own notice.
  • A protest to the appraisal review board is the route when your notice looks higher than local sales support.
  • Rates are adopted in the fall, ahead of bills.

A homestead also carries a 10 percent yearly cap on appraised value, which keeps a rising market from passing straight into the taxable base.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about the economy behind Texas housing demand?
sections.html:
Demand for houses rests on jobs and income, and QuickFacts gives several measures for Texas. Per capita income for 2020 to 2024 is $40,752 in 2024 dollars, and the employer count for 2023 was 670,878 establishments with total employment of 12,012,629.

  • Total employment changed by 4.4% between 2022 and 2023.
  • Annual payroll in 2023 was $805,008,752 thousand.
  • Retail sales in 2022 totaled $608,178,719 thousand, or $20,252 per capita.
  • Employer firms in 2023 numbered 470,732, of which 22,721 were veteran-owned.
  • Households with a broadband subscription: 91.4% for 2020 to 2024.
  • High school graduates or higher among adults 25 and older: 86.0%; bachelor's degree or higher: 33.8%.

None of these converts into a home price, but they show a large, working state where the share of households that own is under two thirds.

sections.h2: What should a Texas seller take from the data?
sections.html:
Use the statewide figures for background and rely on local evidence for pricing. The 2026 quarterly index values show a steady series, and the Census medians describe an owner base that is mostly homeowners, but neither can say what a specific house will fetch or how long it will take to close.

Before taking an offer, pull your appraisal notice and ask the county tax office for the current-year payoff. Because the year's lien attaches on January 1, taxes belong in the closing math even if the bill has not been mailed.

faqs.q: What is the FHFA house price index for Texas?
faqs.a: It was 450.76 not seasonally adjusted and 444.25 seasonally adjusted for the second quarter of 2026, with 1991 Q1 equal to 100. It tracks repeat-sale price changes, not any one home.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Texas?
faqs.a: $283,800 for owner-occupied units in 2020 to 2024, per the Census Bureau. It is a statewide survey median, and local medians differ.

faqs.q: What share of Texans own their homes?
faqs.a: About 62.6%, by the QuickFacts owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024.

faqs.q: Can this data predict where Texas prices are heading?
faqs.a: No. Both sources report history, and neither offers a forecast. Use local comparable sales for pricing a particular house.

faqs.q: When do Texas tax bills arrive?
faqs.a: Around October 1, per the Comptroller's pay page. Anything unpaid on February 1 is delinquent, and a bill mailed after January 10 can push that date back.
